title: Queue priority weights experiment log
content:
Goal:
- Understand a recent throughput regression that correlates with PR 243 (adaptive queuing changes). Suspect interaction between queue priority weights and continuous batching warmup logic causing backlog amplification for low-priority routes.

Background:
- Deployed adaptive-queue v2 (PR 243) on 2024-09-16 to assign dynamic priority weights based on model latency percentiles.
- After deploy, several low-QPS routes saw sudden latency spikes and reduced throughput for bursty traffic. High-priority routes looked fine.

Observations (from 2024-09-16 -> 2024-09-18):
- P95 token latency for route /v1/generate-high dropped from ~120ms to ~115ms (ok).
- P95 for /v1/generate-low increased from ~180ms to ~380ms. Throughput (tokens/s) for low route dropped by ~55%.
- Batching telemetry shows average batch size for low route went from 8->3. Combined avgbatch across worker decreased by ~25%.
- Exported queue snapshots: high-priority queue often fully utilized; low-priority queue had long tail of requests waiting >250ms.

Commands I ran (copied):
- kubectl get pods -n serving | grep runtime
  runtime-abcde-1   2/2   Running   0     7d

- kubectl logs runtime-abcde-1 -c runtime --since=2h | egrep "batch|queue|priority" -B1 -A2\  
  [2024-09-18T14:03:22Z] INFO queue-manager: enqueued req route=/v1/generate-low q=low weight=0.1
  [2024-09-18T14:03:22Z] DEBUG batcher: emitted batch size=2 routes=[/v1/generate-high,/v1/generate-low]
  [2024-09-18T14:03:22Z] WARN queue-manager: starvation-detect low-queue-latency=260ms

- curl -s -X POST $SAMPLE_LOAD --data @payload_low.json -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' | jq '.latency'
  386

- psql -h telemetry-prod -c "select route, avg(batch_size), count(*) from batches where ts > '2024-09-16' group by route;"
  generate_high | 7.9 | 12000
  generate_low  | 3.1 | 5300

Key logs & error snippets:
- "WARN queue-manager: effective-weight for low route dropped from 0.35 -> 0.08 after percentile update"
- "DEBUG batching: preferential-fill: skipped 76 low-priority tokens to avoid latency SLO violation on high route"
- "INFO warmup: continuous-batcher warmup completed=false, warmed_shards=0/4"

Initial hypotheses:
1) Weight floor too low: dynamic algorithm reduces low route weight aggressively when its latency percentiles spike, but because batcher uses cross-route batching to improve efficiency, the low route gets prevented from forming stable batches. Small batches -> poor throughput -> higher latency -> lower weight -> feedback loop.
2) Warmup interaction: continuous-batcher warmup flag gating prevents low routes from participating in cross-batch pooling until warmed_shards threshold met; because weights are low, they never reach warmup triggers.
3) Priority preemption bug: when high queue is busy, the preemption logic consumes free slots from low queue without allowing batch formation (bug in preemption threshold computation).

Experiments and results:
- EXP-1: Increase min_weight for low routes to 0.15 (was 0.05). Deployed to canary (1 pod). 2024-09-19 09:00 -> 2h run.
  Observed: avgbatch low -> 4.8 (up from 3.1), p95 latency low -> 210ms (down from 380ms), throughput +28%. No impact to high route.
  Command: curl -X POST http://canary:8080/admin/config -d '{"min_route_weight":0.15}'

- EXP-2: Force warmup bypass for low route (set continuous-batcher.warmup.enabled=false for route). Canary 2024-09-19 13:00 -> 1h.
  Observed: immediate increase in warmed_shards reported; avgbatch low -> 5.3; p95 low -> 195ms. But noticed CPU usage on canary increased ~6%.

- EXP-3: Temporarily cap high-route priority consumption: cap_preempt_pct=0.6 (from 0.9). 2024-09-20 10:00 -> 3h.
  Observed: low route avgbatch -> 4.2; high route avgbatch down slightly 7.9->7.1; no SLO violations on high. Suggests preemption threshold too permissive.

Quick config snippets tried (copied from runtime-config):
- adaptive_queue: {percentile_window_ms: 30000, adjust_step: 0.05, min_weight: 0.15, max_weight: 0.9}
- continuous_batcher: {warmup: {enabled: true, shards_threshold: 2}, max_batch_delay_ms: 12}
- preemption: {cap_preempt_pct: 0.6, min_free_slots: 2}

What repro steps reliably show the regression locally (mini-produce):
1) Start local runtime with adaptive-queue enabled and default min_weight=0.05.
2) Launch two traffic generators: high_traffic: 20 qps, low_bursty: 0.5 qps with spikes to 12 qps for 5s every 30s.
3) Observe avgbatch and queue depth logged by local batcher; low route avgbatch drops below 3 within ~90s.
4) Repeat with min_weight=0.15 and observe mitigation.

Metrics to collect next run (add to telemetry):
- per-route average batch sizes over 1m/5m windows
- queued request age histogram by priority bucket
- weight history (time series of effective weights per route)
- warmup shard counts per route
- preemption events counter broken down by source route/target route

Open questions / unknowns:
- What's the intended semantics of "min_weight" vs "warmup"? Are they orthogonal or interacting? Need code owner to confirm.
- Is continuous-batcher warmup shard count per-process or cluster-wide? Current logs ambiguous.
- Does preemption do partial drain (take tokens) or whole-request preempt? Logs suggest token-level preemption which hurts small-batch routes.

Immediate recommendations (low-risk):
- Roll min_weight up for low-priority customer routes from 0.05 -> 0.12 cluster-wide (canary shows good improvement).
- Reduce cap_preempt_pct default to 0.7 in prod until we validate further.
- Add explicit warmup bypass flag for routes with <1 rps baseline to avoid starvation during burst spikes.

Next actions / owners:
- Priya: file PR to update min_weight default and add config toggle (INF-4821) — due 2024-09-25.
- Jorge: add telemetry dashboard for weight history + preemption event counters — due 2024-09-27.
- Alex (me): run one-week rolling canary with min_weight=0.12 and cap_preempt_pct=0.7; collect metrics, prepare roll plan — start 2024-09-22.

Notes to self: keep replay seed for local generator saved at /home/alex/dev/serving/tests/priority-seeds/seed-20240918.json. When writing PR, include the microbench results (EXP-1/2/3) and CPU impact note.

Appendix: quick paste of batcher debug toggle output (trimmed)
[2024-09-19T09:14:31Z] DEBUG batcher: route=/v1/generate-low queue_len=7 effective-weight=0.12 avgbatch=4.6 warmup_shards=1
[2024-09-19T09:14:31Z] DEBUG batcher: route=/v1/generate-high queue_len=2 effective-weight=0.88 avgbatch=7.6 warmup_shards=4

End of notes.
